standard_prerequisites.name: The Koszul complex on the n-th powers of a generating set is bounded and its cohomology modules are annihilated by a power of the ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that tensoring the object with those complexes vanishes, by the vanishing statement for modules annihilated by a power of the ideal.

standard_prerequisites.name: A derived complete object is the derived limit of its tensor products with the Koszul complexes of the system
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes that the object itself is zero once all those tensor products vanish.

standard_prerequisites.name: The special case of the boundedness statement for a derived complete object also gives the result, as the author notes at the start
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides an alternative shorter proof, after which the direct proof is given.

core_obligations: Announce that the statement is a special case of the boundedness statement for derived complete objects, but give a direct proof as well (proof lines 26489-26490).
Choose generators of the ideal, let the Koszul complex on their n-th powers be denoted, and record that it is bounded with cohomology annihilated by a power of the ideal (proof lines 26491-26494).
Apply the vanishing statement for modules annihilated by a power of the ideal to conclude that the tensor product of the object with each of these Koszul complexes vanishes (proof lines 26494-26496).
Use the description of a derived complete object as the derived limit of those tensor products to conclude that the object is zero, which proves the statement (proof lines 26496-26500).
proof_roadmap: Note the alternative proof through the boundedness statement, then start the direct one (proof lines 26489-26491).
Kill the tensor products with the Koszul complexes by the vanishing statement (proof lines 26491-26496).
Read the object off as the derived limit of those tensor products and conclude it is zero (proof lines 26496-26500).
difficulty_reason: The statement is the derived Nakayama lemma: for a finitely generated ideal, a derived complete object whose reduction modulo the ideal vanishes must be zero (statement lines 26471-26487). The proof is a direct argument through the Koszul complexes on the powers of a generating set: since those complexes are bounded with cohomology annihilated by a power of the ideal, the vanishing statement for modules annihilated by a power of the ideal kills all tensor products with them, and the description of a derived complete object as the derived limit of precisely those tensor products then forces the object to vanish (proof lines 26489-26500). The two inputs are stated in the proof and the argument is short, but it is a complete derivation rather than a citation chain. The counted statement contains the author's slogan and reference environments; the retained preamble defines both as comment-type, so their bodies and the citation inside them are discarded when the document is typeset, which is why the card needs no bibliography, and the counted span needs the three same-chapter references carried as navigation stubs.
